sections.title: ECG paper and waves
notes: Small square **40 ms**, large square **200 ms**, 300 large squares per minute. Standard: 10 mm amplitude, 25 mm/s.
P: atrial depolarization. PR: AV conduction. QRS: ventricular depolarization. ST and T: repolarization. QT: whole ventricular cycle.

sections.title: Leads and normal variation by age
notes: Lateral: I, aVL, V5, V6. Inferior: II, III, aVF. V1 and V2 see the right ventricle, V5 and V6 the left.
**T wave upright in V1 is normal only in the first week**, then suggests RV hypertrophy (normal again after about 6 to 7 years).
Newborns: big R in V1 that shrinks with age.

sections.title: Systematic approach, rate and axis
notes: Order: rhythm, rate, axis, P wave and PR, QRS, QT, ST, T.
Rate: **300 divided by large squares between R waves** (or R waves in 10 seconds times 6).
Axis from I and aVF: both positive normal, I positive aVF negative **left**, I negative aVF positive **right**. **Newborns normally have right axis deviation**.

sections.title: Atrial enlargement
notes: **Tall peaked P over 3 mm** in II: right atrial enlargement.
**Broad notched P over 120 ms** in II or deep negative P in V1: left atrial enlargement.

sections.title: PR interval and heart block
notes: PR under 200 ms (under 130 ms in newborns).
**First degree**: long PR, every P conducts. **Mobitz I (Wenckebach)**: PR lengthens until a dropped QRS. **Mobitz II**: normal PR, sudden dropped QRS.
**Third degree**: P and QRS independent, bradycardia (e.g. after heart surgery).

sections.title: Heart block management
notes: Observe first degree and Mobitz I.

Mobitz II and complete block with symptomatic bradycardia: **transcutaneous or transvenous pacing**. **Atropine is the wrong answer for complete heart block** (can worsen it). Permanent pacemaker may be needed.

sections.title: QRS: ventricular hypertrophy
notes: QRS normally under 120 ms. Always compare to **age norms**.
**Tall R in V1 and deep S in V6**: right ventricular hypertrophy. Deep S in V1 and tall R in V6: left ventricular hypertrophy.

sections.title: Right bundle branch block
notes: Common in kids **after open heart surgery** (repaired tetralogy).
**Wide QRS over 120 ms with RSR' in V1**, wide S in V6.

sections.title: Premature atrial and ventricular contractions
notes: **PACs**: early beat with an odd P wave and normal QRS. Very common in newborns. **Reassure**, avoid caffeine.
**PVCs**: early beat with **no P and a wide bizarre QRS**. Benign if **uniform, suppressed by exercise**, normal heart, no family history of sudden death.
Refer: multiform PVCs, **worse with exercise**, structural disease, family history, or symptoms. Can be first sign of myocarditis.

sections.title: QT interval and long QT
notes: **QTc = QT / square root of RR** (in seconds). Normal up to 0.44 s (up to 0.49 s under 6 months).
Case: teen faints **playing football**, QT more than half the RR: **long QT**.
Causes: **tricyclics**, macrolides, TMP-SMX, **low calcium, magnesium, potassium**, ion channel genes.

sections.title: Long QT syndromes and treatment
notes: **Jervell and Lange-Nielsen: long QT with congenital deafness**. Romano-Ward: no deafness.
Ask about family sudden death and deafness. Fainting with **swimming, startle, exercise**, seizures, 10% sudden arrest.
Newborn fails hearing screen with very long QT: **Jervell and Lange-Nielsen**. Treat with **beta blockers**, ICD for high risk, avoid QT-prolonging drugs.

sections.title: Atrial flutter
notes: **Sawtooth** flutter waves (II, III, aVF), atrial rate 300 to 400, usually 2:1 conduction, regular RR.
Infants: heart failure. Over 24 to 48 hours: risk of atrial clot.
**Synchronized cardioversion** if no clot (or if unstable). Chronic: anticoagulate 2 to 4 weeks first. Ablation can cure.

sections.title: Atrial fibrillation
notes: **Irregularly irregular**, no clear P waves.
Causes: other SVTs, **hyperthyroidism**, low magnesium, **cocaine**, HCM, ASD.
Urgent cardiology. Unstable: synchronized cardioversion.

sections.title: Supraventricular tachycardia
notes: **Narrow complex**, fixed rate with **no beat-to-beat variation**, P waves hidden in the T.
Infants: **220 to 270**, poor feeding, irritability, heart failure if prolonged. Children 180 to 240, palpitations. A crying baby at 180 that settles is not SVT.
Stable: **vagal manoeuvres (ice to the face)**, then **IV adenosine**. **No verapamil under 1 year** (shock). No digoxin in WPW. Unstable: **synchronized cardioversion**. Recurrent: ablation.

sections.title: Wolff-Parkinson-White
notes: Accessory pathway: **short PR, delta wave, wide QRS**.
Associated with **Ebstein anomaly**, cardiomyopathy, corrected transposition.

sections.title: Tricyclic overdose ECG
notes: Sinus tachycardia, long PR, QRS and QTc.
**QRS over 100 ms: give sodium bicarbonate**.

sections.title: Ventricular tachycardia
notes: 3 or more beats of **wide bizarre QRS**, regular, T opposite the QRS.
Causes: drugs (**decongestants**, caffeine), electrolytes, heart disease, post-surgery, cardiomyopathy.
**Emergency**: check stability first. Then echo, stress test, Holter.

sections.title: Ventricular fibrillation
notes: Chaotic waves, no P or QRS, **no pulse**. Start ACLS and **defibrillate (unsynchronized)**.

sections.title: ST elevation: pericarditis
notes: Chest pain worse **lying flat and with inspiration**, **diffuse ST elevation in all leads**: pericarditis.
Focal ST changes: rare ischemia (anomalous coronary, familial hypercholesterolemia).

sections.title: T waves and sinus arrhythmia
notes: **Peaked T waves: hyperkalemia** (then long PR, lost P, wide QRS as potassium rises). Flat T: hypokalemia, hypothyroidism.
**Sinus arrhythmia**: rate rises with inspiration, falls with expiration. Normal, reassure.
